s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive enlargement and discomfort of a digit with associated neurological symptoms and limited mobility
salient_findings: Enlargement of the left middle finger since birth
Limited flexion of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints
key_facts: The patient is a 14-year-old girl
The left middle finger has been larger than the others since birth
The finger has grown progressively over time
The patient developed tingling at the fingertip 3 months before presentation
There is limited flexion of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints
The overlying skin of the enlarged finger is normal
There is tenderness throughout the enlargement
Sensation is decreased distally
Laboratory studies were unremarkable
A CT scan of the hand showed overgrowth of the phalanges and surrounding soft tissue

shortlist.label: Macrodactyly
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's finger has been larger than the others since birth and has grown progressively, which is consistent with macrodactyly

shortlist.label: Lipofibromatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: The CT scan showed overgrowth of the phalanges and surrounding soft tissue, suggesting a lipomatous process, which is consistent with lipofibromatous hamartoma

shortlist.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are also consistent with fibrolipomatous hamartoma, a condition characterized by overgrowth of fibrous and fatty tissue

shortlist.label: Maffucci syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, Maffucci syndrome is a rare condition that can cause progressive enlargement of a digit, and it should be considered in the differential diagnosis

shortlist.label: Ollier disease
shortlist.why_kept: Ollier disease is another rare condition that can cause skeletal abnormalities, including overgrowth of a digit, and it should be considered in the differential diagnosis

raw.rationale: The CT scan showing overgrowth of the phalanges and surrounding soft tissue, along with the clinical presentation of a progressively enlarging finger since birth and normal overlying skin, is consistent with fibrolipomatous hamartoma, a benign tumor composed of fibrous and fatty tissue.

rejected.label: Macrodactyly
rejected.why: While macrodactyly refers to an enlarged digit, it is more of a descriptive term rather than a specific diagnosis and does not account for the specific tissue overgrowth seen on the CT scan.

rejected.label: Lipofibromatous hamartoma
rejected.why: This is a less commonly used term and seems to be related to or synonymous with fibrolipomatous hamartoma, but the specific details provided in the case are more closely aligned with the characteristics of fibrolipomatous hamartoma.

rejected.label: Maffucci syndrome
rejected.why: Maffucci syndrome involves multiple enchondromas and hemangiomas, which were not indicated in the case presentation.

rejected.label: Ollier disease
rejected.why: Ollier disease is characterized by multiple enchondromas, which were not mentioned in the case, and typically does not present with the specific type of soft tissue overgrowth described.
